newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to pick Handlowy sale consortium this week.
newsitem.headline: Poland to pick Handlowy sale consortium this week.

text.p: This week Poland should pick a banking consortium to arrange the planned June public offering of Bank Handlowy SA shares, a deputy finance minister said.
"From Monday on we will be holding intensive talks on the choice of banks that will co-arrange the offering of Bank Handlowy," Karol Szwarc told Reuters in a Monday interview.
"These talks should be concluded within a week," he added.
Karol Szwarc said that under the privatisation plan the public offering due in late June would be divided equally into institutional and retail tranches.

The shares would represent 30 percent equity in the bank after a planned 112 million zloty share capital increase to facilitate a convertible bond issue designed to help finance Poland's social security reform.
"We plan the public offering for late June, which will encompass 30 percent of shares (after the bond issue) with about 15 percent stakes offered institutional and small investors," Szwarc said.
Before the public offering Bank Handlowy is due to offer 42.9 percent of its present shares to a group of selected international financial institutions but Szwarc would not give any details.

Szwarc said that by the end of this month the government was also likely to decide on the privatisation timetable of another large Polish bank Pekao SA, which now leads a group of four state-owned banks.
He added that next year the government planned to privatise Bank Zachodni SA.
He said privatisation of the largest savings bank Powszechna Kasa Oszczednosci BP (PKO BP) would begin before 2000.
"We have agreed that the privatisation of PKO BP, Poland's largest retail bank, would start before 2000," Szwarc said.
Earlier the government has said the bank's privatisation had to wait until after 2000 because of a large proportion of bad housing loans in its portfolio.
